denial_rate_notes: No single published denial rate for California UI initial claims. Documented components: EDD denied about 3.4 million pandemic-era claims under UIC § 1253(a) for non-response (G2); ALJs overturn about 50 percent of appealed EDD decisions, implying 5-10 percent of all applicants are denied by EDD before being approved by an ALJ (G2, 'Half of EDD Decisions Overturned on Appeal'); EDD's own weekly legislative reports counted only about 705,000 'disqualified/denied' over the same period (G2).

known_gaps: The routing rule is not public. G3 proves an internal report called "CPT Conditions" enumerates every reason an electronic claim is diverted to manual review, and names one code (CPT Code 023, international mailing address), but neither the current condition list nor the code-to-queue mapping is published anywhere. A10/A06/A07 are therefore correct in existence but unscored in structure: a solver cannot recover the branch conditions, and neither can this gold file.

No gold document states which of the three fact-finding channels (Eligibility Questionnaire / DE 4365FF / phone interview) a given claim gets, or the lead time for scheduling a phone interview. D8 lists all three and gives day counts only for the questionnaire path (3 days + 7 days).

No gold document states an internal service level for the interval between the eligibility interview (A22) and the determination (A23). A widely repeated claimant report of "10 business days after the interview" appears in at least three independent Reddit threads and in no EDD, Auditor, or LAO document we hold; it is deliberately excluded from this gold file.

Current-era numbers are missing. The manual-review share (40 percent), automation rate (~60 percent), tier 1 / EPR staffing split, and identity-verification throughput all come from 2020-2022 documents. Nothing equivalent has been published for the post-EDDNext system, so A05-A07 timing is dated rather than current.

A05 is modelled as a single system activity, but G1's Figure 1 is EDD's own simplification of its procedure documents; the underlying sequence (wage-record retrieval, base-period computation, SSA/DMV identity matching, claim establishment) is not separately documented, so the gold undercounts activities inside the automated path.

Occasion coding is lossy for this process: the phone interview (A22) and the ALJ hearing (A31) are both conducted by telephone, but the schema's occasion enum has no telephone value, so A22 is coded 'internal' and A31 'hearing'.

Per-activity timing distributions do not exist anywhere. Every timing figure in this file is either a statutory or federal deadline, an agency-wide average, or a compliance-rate threshold; no gold document publishes stage-level medians or p90s for California UI, so p90_days is null for most activities.

Observed-tier evidence about EDD is itself unreliable: G1 found EDD's public backlog dashboard reported about 685,700 claims while fewer than 20,000 actually had incomplete EDD work, and G2 found EDD's legislative reporting undercounted true denials roughly fivefold. Any solver scored against EDD's own published statistics is being scored against a known-biased instrument.

Title 22 CCR §§ 1256-1, 1256-3, 1256-30, 1253(c)-1 and 1326-6(b)(2) govern determination substance and are cited secondhand in G5 but were not fetched, so the determination step (A23) has no regulation-level element_ref.
Judicial review (writ of mandate, within six months of the Appeals Board decision per G4) is documented but excluded from the activity list as outside the implementer's process.
notes: Gold for the (ui_claim, EDD) task. Designed-tier spine: G1's Figure 1 (drawn by the Auditor from EDD's own procedure documents) for the automated-vs-manual filing fork; G3 for the manual-review queues, the CPT Conditions report, the ID.me procurement and the BPO/UI-Online (EDDCAN) account-linking defect; G2 for what makes eligibility hard to prove and for appeal overturn rates; G4 (DE 1433, CUIAB's own procedure manual) for the entire appeal lane; G5 for determination and appeal timeliness baselines; G6 for the internal fraud-triage units. Declared EDD step pages (D1-D10) are used only to anchor the applicant-facing activities and to fix which steps a claimant can actually see, per the brief. Visibility discipline: an activity is labelled staff_only only after checking that no applicant-facing document in corpus/realworld/ui_claim/raw/ mentions it. The four staff_only activities are A05 (automatic claim establishment; 'automatic' appears in no applicant-facing UI page, only in two unrelated passages of DE 1275A, about direct-deposit transfers and alternate claim types), A06 (CPT routing; 'manual', 'queue' and 'CPT' appear in no applicant-facing page), A11 (fraud triage units; the unit names appear only in G6), and A16 (RESEA automated profiling; 'reemployment' and 'RESEA' appear in no applicant-facing page, only in UIC § 1253(f)). A07 and A19 are applicant_inferable rather than staff_only because D6 tells the claimant that a 'Pending' status means EDD is confirming identity or eligibility. CUIAB registration and calendaring (A28, A29) are applicant_inferable because D9 tells the claimant the appeal is forwarded and a hearing will be scheduled, even though the FIFO-with-eligibility-priority rule exists only in G4. Two known gold-error risks: (1) the timing_gold end-to-end figure is EDD's own declared estimate, which happens to coincide with the federal nonwaiting-week benchmark rather than with measured California performance (G1 reports 61-75 percent within 14 days); (2) all back-office structure is 2020-2022 vintage and EDDNext has since changed the systems, so this gold is a snapshot of the audited process, not necessarily the 2026 process.
